quick: 1000 mg IV once (>=50 kg); 20 mg/kg if <50 kg
Avoid 1st trimester; use only if clearly needed thereafter
Indicated in non-dialysis CKD; no dose change
Avoid in hepatic dysfunction with iron overload
summary: Iron isomaltoside 1000 (ferric derisomaltose, Monoferric) is an intravenous iron-carbohydrate complex for iron deficiency anemia in adults intolerant of or unresponsive to oral iron, and in non-dialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease. A full replacement dose of up to 1000 mg can be given as a single infusion over at least 20 minutes (20 mg/kg if under 50 kg). The main risk is serious hypersensitivity, so patients are observed for at least 30 minutes after dosing.
indications: Iron deficiency anemia in adults intolerant of oral iron or with unsatisfactory response to oral iron
Iron deficiency anemia in adults with non-hemodialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease (NDD-CKD)

dosage.d: 1000 mg elemental iron as a single IV infusion over at least 20 minutes
dosage.n: Repeat if iron deficiency anemia recurs

dosage.d: 20 mg/kg actual body weight as a single IV infusion over at least 20 minutes
dosage.n: Each mL contains 100 mg elemental iron

dosage.d: Repeat replacement dose when anemia and iron deficiency recur
dosage.n: Base on hemoglobin, ferritin and TSAT

admin: Administer only where staff and resuscitation facilities for hypersensitivity reactions are immediately available
Inspect for particulate matter and discoloration before use
Infuse over at least 20 minutes; may dilute in 0.9% sodium chloride
Observe the patient for at least 30 minutes after each administration
Avoid extravasation - can cause persistent brown skin staining
moa: Ferric derisomaltose is a complex of iron(III) hydroxide and derisomaltose (an iron-carbohydrate oligosaccharide). The matrix allows controlled, slow release of bioavailable iron, which binds to transferrin for transport to erythroid precursor cells and incorporation into hemoglobin, replenishing depleted iron stores while limiting free (labile) iron release.

absolute: History of serious hypersensitivity to the product or any component
Iron overload or disturbances in iron utilization (e.g., hemochromatosis)
Anemia not caused by iron deficiency
relative: Known allergy or asthma/atopy (higher hypersensitivity risk)
monitor: Signs of hypersensitivity during and after infusion

preg: No adequate human data; iron complexes have been teratogenic/embryocidal in non-iron-depleted animals. Avoid in the first trimester; use later in pregnancy only if clearly needed, as maternal hypersensitivity reactions can harm the fetus. Untreated IDA also carries maternal-fetal risk.
lact: Transfer of intravenous iron into breast milk is negligible and oral absorption by the infant is minimal; it is considered compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: Specifically indicated for iron deficiency anemia in non-hemodialysis-dependent CKD; no dose adjustment for renal function is required. It is not indicated for dialysis-dependent CKD in the US label.
hepatic: Use with caution; avoid in patients with hepatic dysfunction where iron overload may be a precipitating factor. Parenteral iron should be given only when benefit outweighs risk.

major: Concomitant oral iron - reduces oral iron absorption; withhold oral iron during and for a period after IV iron
moderate: Other parenteral iron products - risk of cumulative iron overload
minor: Dimercaprol / chelators - may interact with iron handling
interactions.food: Not relevant; given intravenously. Stop oral iron supplements while on IV iron.
interactions.diagnostics: Can transiently raise serum ferritin and falsely elevate serum iron/TSAT for days to weeks; may interfere with iron-status interpretation shortly after dosing.

rare: Persistent brown skin staining from extravasation
emergency: Anaphylaxis with hypotension, collapse or loss of consciousness

monitoring: Hemoglobin, serum ferritin and transferrin saturation to guide and confirm response
Continuous observation for hypersensitivity during and for >=30 minutes after infusion
Serum phosphate if repeated dosing or symptoms of hypophosphatemia
counsel: This is a one-time (or occasional) iron infusion given in a monitored setting
Tell staff immediately if you feel flushing, chest tightness, breathlessness, dizziness or itching
You will be watched for at least 30 minutes after the infusion
Stop taking oral iron tablets unless your doctor tells you otherwise
A small skin stain can occur if the drug leaks at the injection site
pk: Reticulocyte response within days; hemoglobin rises over 1-4 weeks
Iron is taken up by reticuloendothelial system shortly after infusion
Single replacement dose can correct deficit; effect persists for weeks
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); do not freeze; use diluted solution within 8 h
pearls: A full course (up to 1000 mg) can be given in one rapid infusion - an advantage over older IV irons
Serious hypersensitivity is the key risk; ensure resuscitation readiness and 30-minute post-dose observation
Do not use in iron overload or non-iron-deficiency anemia
Watch for hypophosphatemia with parenteral iron-carbohydrate complexes
Ferritin/TSAT are unreliable for a few weeks after dosing
missed: Not applicable in the usual sense - dosing is per episode of iron deficiency anemia rather than a fixed daily schedule. If a planned infusion is missed, reschedule with the treating team.
overdose: Excessive dosing can cause accumulation of iron in storage sites leading to hemosiderosis/hemochromatosis. Avoid in iron overload. Manage accumulation with iron-status monitoring and, if severe, iron chelation therapy.
